notes.17: 23% of candidates chose the correct answer, A. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C, chosen by 40% of candidates. Choice C was magnesium, but magnesium chloride solution produces a white precipitate with NaOH(aq) that is insoluble in excess alkali and therefore will not give a solution.. The correct 9701 Chemistry November 2014 answer was aluminium, A. Aluminium chloride solution will give a white precipitate with NaOH(aq) that dissolves in excess alkali.

There are five isomers of C H O that are aldehydes: pentanal, the two optical isomers of 2- 5 10 methylbutanal, 3-methylbutanal, and dimethylpropanal. Candidates choosing B may not have appreciated that 2-methylbutanal exists as a pair of optical isomers.
notes.27: 40% of candidates chose the correct answer, B. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was C, chosen by 45% of candidates. The reaction described is the substitution of CN for Br, followed by the hydrolysis of CN to COOH. The starting material must therefore have one carbon atom less than the final product given in the question.
notes.29: 36% of candidates chose the correct answer, B. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was D, chosen by 32% of candidates. These figures suggest that the majority of candidates knew that the cyclohexyl rings, for example, are non-planar. Those choosing D also believed that cholesterol displays cis-trans isomerism at the double bond. This is not possible where the double bond is constrained within a ring system.
notes.30: 21% of candidates chose the correct answer, C. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was A, chosen by 39% of candidates. Candidates should be reminded that in questions such as this, they are advised to draw skeletal or structural formulae in order to work out the correct answer.
notes.39: 43% of candidates chose the correct answer, D. The most commonly chosen incorrect answer was B, chosen by 35% of candidates. The key to the question is the words “coloured organic product”. Ethanal undergoes a condensation reaction with 2,4-DNPH, giving an organic product which is an orange precipitate, so statement 1 is a correct answer. When ethanol is oxidised by acidified potassium dichromate(VI) a colour change is seen, but the organic products, ethanal and ethanoic acid, are colourless, so statement 2 is not a correct answer.
